questions.question_text: How many bookings were made on Wednesday? $\begin{array}{c|rrrr}\text{Day}&\text{Mon}&\text{Tue}&\text{Wed}&\text{Thu}\\\hline\text{Bookings}&42&38&51&47\end{array}$

options.why: Reads the Tuesday value instead of the Wednesday value.
Reads the Thursday value instead of the Wednesday value.
Adds all four days instead of reading the requested single value.

questions.question_text: Find the total number of workshop places. $\begin{array}{c|rrrr}\text{Workshop}&A&B&C&D\\\hline\text{Places}&16&24&18&22\end{array}$

options.why: Adds only three values and omits Workshop A.
Adds only the first two workshop values.
Reports the largest single value instead of the total.
Reads the Central bar instead of the South bar.
Reads the North bar instead of the South bar.
Reports the number of grid steps and ignores the scale of 15.

questions.solution_text: The South bar reaches the label $75$.

options.why: Adds the grid-step heights but does not apply the scale of eight.
Reports only the largest bar instead of adding all four bars.
Uses 16, 40, 24 and 24, misreading the fourth bar by one interval.

questions.question_text: The total is $200$. Find the missing value. $\begin{array}{c|rrrr}\text{Zone}&A&B&C&D\\\hline\text{Requests}&48&57&39&?\end{array}$

options.why: Finds the subtotal of known values but does not subtract it from 200.
Subtracts an incorrect known subtotal of 156 from the total.
Adds the known subtotal to 200 instead of finding the missing part.

questions.question_text: A table shows values $22$, $31$ and $27$. A separate line graph shows values $20$, $25$ and $30$. Which total is larger?

options.text: The table total is larger by $5$
The line-graph total is larger by $5$
options.why: Finds the difference but reverses which display has the larger total.
Compares only the middle values and ignores the other observations.

options.text: The table total is larger by $10$
options.why: Uses only the difference between 30 and 20 rather than comparing the totals.
